children: The dollar's rise toward 160 yen brings intervention risk back into focus, MUFG Bank's Lloyd Chan says in a research report. "Japanese officials signalled greater coordination with the U.S. against rapid, one-sided yen depreciation," the senior currency analyst says. "This should provide some resistance to further USD/JPY upside, but a sustained yen recovery ultimately requires further BOJ normalisation and a narrower U.S.-Japan rate differential," the analyst adds. The dollar is 0.1% higher at 159.77 yen after touching 160.18 yen on Friday, the highest intraday level since early September, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
